title: urn:qauth:realm-file:v1-rc.0
description: The declarative realm file, format urn:qauth:realm-file:v1-rc.0: a realm's configuration, without any secret value (ADR-018 §5). Generated from libs/fastify/realm-file; the docs page reference/realm-file describes every section, its natural key and the rules of growth. A member this schema does not name is refused, a section of a later release included, and so is a URL with a user name or password.

format.description: The file's format. Optional: a file without it is read as urn:qauth:realm-file:v1-rc.0. A breaking change raises its release-candidate number before QAuth 1.0.0, and its major version after.

realm.description: The name of the realm the file describes. It only advises: the caller of an import chooses the target realm, and a different name is a warning, so a sandbox realm's file can go to its live realm.

policies.title: QAuth realm policies
policies.description: The realm's policies, in the shape of the policies of the admin API's realm representation, without the <name>Set flag of a secret field: groups of camelCase fields, each matched by its path. A field left out takes its default.

accessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long an access token for a staging or production client is valid, in seconds, at most 86400 (a day).

developmentAccessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long an access token for a development client is valid, in seconds, at most 86400 (a day); no staging or production client receives it.

refreshTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long a refresh token is valid, in seconds, at most 7776000 (90 days), from its issue; a browser-based client's rotated token (a public client with an `https` redirect URI) never outlives the one it replaces, so its family ends with its first (RFC 10017).

adminAccessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long an access token for the admin API is valid, in seconds, at most 900, so a token whose audience is the admin API never lives longer, whatever the other lifetimes say (ADR-019 Decision 7: admin tokens are short-lived).

requireVerifiedAccount.description: Whether the legacy login routes (`POST /auth/login`, `POST /ui/login`) refuse an unverified account's right password with the answer a wrong password gets; the Interaction API verifies such an account inline with an emailed code, whatever this says.

allowSignUp.description: Whether a person may create a new account through the hosted sign-in, from an unknown upstream identity (#639) or with `prompt=create` (#640, for a client whose `hosted_flows` name `register`), or through the legacy `POST /auth/register` (since 0.2.1; it answers 403 while this is off).

newFactorWindowDays.description: How many days, 0 to 30, a passkey or authenticator app bound after a sign-in that proved only the password stays new: the password alone may remove it, and it does not count as the account's strongest factor for a reset or a change; 0 means no window.

minLength.description: The fewest characters (Unicode code points, after NFC normalisation) a new password may have, from 8 to 64; below 15 is a recorded deviation from NIST SP 800-63B-4 while a password can be the only factor.

minScore.description: The lowest zxcvbn strength score, from 0 to 4, a new password may have.

breachListSource.description: Which breach list new and presented passwords are checked against: off (the default), a list the operator supplies, or a k-anonymity range lookup through the egress client that sends only the first five hex characters of the password's SHA-1; a failed check never blocks a sign-in.

enabled.description: Whether repeated failed sign-ins for one identifier lock it out for a while; when off, failures are only logged.

maxAttempts.description: How many failed sign-ins within the window lock an identifier out.

windowSeconds.description: The window, in seconds, over which failed sign-ins are counted, at most 86400 (a day).

lockoutSeconds.description: How long, in seconds, a locked-out identifier is refused before any password check, at most 86400 (a day).

requiredAtSignUp.description: Whether every `prompt=create` registration passes the bot challenge before its address is asked for, whatever the client; it then needs JavaScript, a client that cannot serve the challenge cannot register, and the legacy `POST /auth/register` ignores it.

difficulty.description: How many leading zero bits the built-in proof of work asks for; each one doubles the work of the page that solves it, and 18 takes a browser a second or two.

offerAfterSignIn.description: Whether the hosted sign-in offers to add a passkey after a password sign-in, to a verified account whose only factor is that password, while passkeys are on (`WEBAUTHN_ENABLED`); a passkey added from the account page is not affected.

errorPage.description: The path on the realm origin, under `/ui/`, of the ceremony app’s page for the endings that leave no interaction to show (a provider callback whose sign-in has ended, the logout’s own pages), or null to keep the auth server’s own pages.

dynamicRegistrationAllowedScopes.description: The scopes a dynamically registered client may hold; a scope outside the list is dropped from the registration, and no scope of the reserved qauth: namespace can be listed.

enabled.description: Whether an HTTPS URL is accepted as a client_id, its metadata fetched from that URL (Client ID Metadata Documents).

trustPolicy.description: Which hosts a metadata-document client_id may have: any HTTPS host, or only the trusted domains.

trustedDomains.description: The hosts the allowlist policy accepts, stored in lower case; an entry `*.example.com` accepts every subdomain of `example.com` but not `example.com` itself.

provider.description: Which transport sends the realm mail: mock (logs only), resend or smtp.

fromAddress.description: The address the realm mail is sent from.

fromName.description: The sender name the realm mail shows.

host.description: The SMTP server the smtp transport connects to.

port.description: The port of the SMTP server.

secure.description: Whether the SMTP connection uses TLS from its start.

user.description: The user name the smtp transport signs in with.

verificationTokenExpirySeconds.description: How long a verification link is valid, in seconds, at least one hour.

invalidateExistingTokensOnResend.description: Whether sending a new verification link makes the earlier ones invalid, so only the latest works.

maxEnvironmentLaxity.description: The laxest environment profile a client of the realm may get; a client set to a laxer one gets this one.

twoAdminMandatoryOperations.description: The admin operations that need a second admin approval in this realm, by operation id.

workloadIssuers.description: The CI issuers whose workload tokens the operator realm exchanges for a service account admin token, with the audience, subject and service account of each.

items.description: A public JWK. A member of private key material (d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, oth, k, priv) is refused: a realm file holds no secret value.

environment.description: The client's environment profile (ADR-008): development, staging or production. Left out, the client is production, the fail-safe default; the realm's posture.maxEnvironmentLaxity caps it. A sandbox realm's client says staging here.

clients.description: The operator-managed OAuth clients, each a seed-manifest client with its OAuth metadata names (RFC 7591) and an optional environment, matched by client_id.

cimd_clients.description: The operator's grants to Client ID Metadata Document clients: the scopes each may receive, those the client_credentials grant may issue it and its audience, matched by client_id. Its document owns every other field.

resources.description: The realm's protected resources: each one's resource indicator (RFC 8707), the scopes it defines with their consent texts, and who may ask for them, matched by resource.

items.description: A public JWK. A member of private key material (d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, oth, k, priv) is refused: a realm file holds no secret value.

first_party_reason.default: QAuth's developer portal: the web front-end this deployment runs for its own developers.

system_client.description: The developer portal's system client, as the migration runner provisions it: its redirect URIs, its public keys and its first-party reason, matched by client_id.
